# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 26 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Thanksgiving Hymns Column 26 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 26:3 — "God of compassion" word order

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God-of compassion" | Hyphenated construct El harachamim |
| LOGOS | "God of compassion" | Standard English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "compassionate God" | Adjectival restructuring |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "God of compassion" preserves the Hebrew construct form in natural English. PNEUMA's restructuring loses the noun-based theology.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:9 — "son of Your handmaid" vs. "son of Your maidservant" vs. "child of Your servant"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-son-of Your handmaid" | Literal ben 'amatekha (cf. Ps 86:16) |
| LOGOS | "the son of Your maidservant" | "Maidservant" as formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the child of Your servant" | Gender-neutral simplification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Maidservant" preserves the feminine Hebrew noun ('amah) and the psalmic allusion to Psalm 86:16. PNEUMA's "servant" loses the specific gender reference.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:14 — "thing of spittle" vs. "spit and molded clay" — extreme self-abasement

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a thing-of spittle, pinched-off clay" | Two separate terms preserved literally |
| LOGOS | "a thing of spittle, a form of pinched clay" | Expanded with nominal frame |
| PNEUMA | "spit and molded clay" | Compressed rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "A thing of spittle, a form of pinched clay" gives each term its own nominal phrase, preserving the rhetorical accumulation of the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:15 — "desire" vs. "longing" vs. "deepest craving" — human orientation toward dust

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his desire is for the-dust" | Literal teshukato |
| LOGOS | "his longing is for the dust" | "Longing" as a more evocative synonym |
| PNEUMA | "our deepest craving is to return to dust" | Expanded first-person plural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Longing" aptly captures the paradoxical desire-for-dissolution expressed by teshukah. PNEUMA's expansion adds "return" and shifts person without warrant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:20 — "revealed" vs. "disclosed" vs. "whispered" — mode of divine revelation to dust

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You have revealed to the-ear-of dust" | Literal galita le-'ozen 'afar |
| LOGOS | "You have disclosed to the ear of dust" | "Disclosed" as formal synonym |
| PNEUMA | "You whispered into the ear of dust" | "Whispered" adds intimacy to the revelation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Disclosed" accurately renders the Hebrew glh without adding the interpretive specificity of PNEUMA's "whispered." The Hebrew does not specify the mode of revelation, only the fact of it.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:21 — "engraved" vs. "inscribed" vs. "etched" — writing on the heart

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You have engraved eternal things" | "Engraved" implies permanence |
| LOGOS | "You have inscribed eternal things" | "Inscribed" — standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "You etched things that last forever" | "Etched" with paraphrased object |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Inscribed" is consistent with 25:15 and the project's standard rendering. "Eternal things" preserved as the direct object.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
